figmaExecutionNotes: Use a light theme across the page with strong trust-first hierarchy.
Do not use a full-grid layout inside feature sections; use readable card rows and balanced columns only.
Maintain consistent section padding and card radius across all feature blocks.
Hero should include a human face element appropriate for enterprise B2B and should not be a generated decorative visual overlay.
Keep trust logos/badges visually dominant immediately after hero.
If optional sections are not supported by finalized content, remove them rather than placeholdering.
For mobile, stack hero content and convert all multi-column sections to single column with clear vertical spacing.
Keep the top strip fixed in the desktop frame and design the page flow beneath it.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected asymmetrical hero: a large left-aligned editorial content block over a soft mesh-gradient field, with a layered right-side floating product collage that overlaps the hero edge. Keep the product UI realistic and crisp, with a marquee trust strip beneath the headline and compact proof chips near the visual. Add subtle grid lines and a few soft red orb accents for depth, but keep the overall look white, clean, and enterprise-trustworthy. CTA must be solid Zoho red with rounded corners. Follow with alternating feature sections that switch left/right and dark/light, including one dark band with light text for security or insight to satisfy contrast and hierarchy.

repetitionBreakers: Open with a split hero that is product-first on the right and continuity-led on the left
Use a static logo grid immediately after hero to establish trust without adding friction
Switch the first product block to a tabs-with-preview layout to handle many features without a flat card grid
Alternate into a split-panel feature section to break the tab rhythm and add visual contrast
Use a spotlight-plus-grid structure for the integrations section to keep dense content scannable
Reserve testimonials for a carousel-static treatment to avoid repeating the same card rhythm
End with a centered lead form card to create a clean conversion pause after proof and pricing
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprise Email and Collaboration
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace for enterprises: unified email, chat, docs, meetings, storage, and AI-powered collaboration with trusted business logos, clear pricing, and a fast Get started CTA.

sections.backgroundTreatment: clean white field with subtle precision-line accents and a structured product mockup panel
sections.designNote: Hero must answer the quality-check trio immediately: headline states what this is, subheadline clarifies it is for enterprise teams, and a single solid red Get started button provides the next step. Keep copy concise and continuity-aligned to the ad message. Right side should show a realistic Zoho Workplace workspace collage with mail, chat, documents, meetings, and storage. Add a compact trust badge cluster beneath the CTA, but keep the hero content-first and crisp.

Use 3-6 recognizable enterprise/customer logos in a clean static flex-wrap grid. If the final logo list is weak in production, replace it with a compact metrics strip anchored by 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally'. Keep this section tight and immediate so warm traffic sees proof before deeper evaluation.

This page has 5+ features across multiple product blocks, so do not use a flat static grid. Start with a tabs-with-preview section focused on the click-driving benefits: unified workspace, real-time collaboration, mobility, and AI assistant Zia. Then alternate into a split-panel section for remaining business-scale and communication capabilities. Final product block should use spotlight-plus-grid for integrations and performance proof, with one strong preview and shorter supporting items. Keep the section rhythm varied and editorial, not template-like.

Optional support section should be visually lighter and more service-oriented, but only if needed to maintain flow. Since trust is already handled early, this section should not compete with product proof. Keep it concise and utility-led, with simple icon cards or counters rather than a dense narrative block.

Use a single highlighted enterprise plan card with a clear feature list and a solid Get started button in accent red. The pricing block should feel calm and straightforward, not promotional. This is a decision-support section, so emphasize included capabilities, migration assistance, storage, and device support.

There are 5 testimonials, so use a static carousel or spotlight slider rather than a dense grid. Lead with operational outcomes: streamlined communication, reduced tool switching, improved collaboration, and faster setup. Keep typography large enough for readability and maintain a restrained editorial feel.

End with a centered conversion card to create a strong closing pause. Keep the form minimal because warm traffic should be guided, not pressured. Primary CTA must remain Get started, solid accent red, full-width on mobile. Reinforce the free trial offer as a low-friction final step.

If a media/logos section is retained, keep it static and minimal. Do not use a marquee unless explicitly required. This section should only act as a closing credibility layer, not an attention magnet.

blueprint.designPersonality: Modern editorial enterprise with calm white space, strong proof hierarchy, subtle shadows, rounded cards, and a clean red accent system. The page should feel dependable, efficient, and globally credible, with logos leading trust and the product experience presented like a polished business suite rather than a generic software template.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a crisp enterprise product mockup or UI collage showing mail, chat, docs, calendar, and analytics in one workspace. Keep the hero visual clean and realistic, not generated or illustrative. Make logos the dominant trust signal through a static logo grid and compact proof badges.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is medium-long and needs to stay strong without wrapping awkwardly; 56px gives enterprise presence while preserving balance in a split hero layout.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero banner with brand logo at top, large centered headline, short supporting subcopy, and a compact bullet list of key benefits; strong above-the-fold emphasis with minimal competing elements.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero-first layout followed by a lead-capture form card, then stacked content sections with repeated headline/description blocks and feature lists; linear long-form scroll with progressive disclosure rather than dense multi-column dashboards.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content cards/forms with clear borders or subtle separation, functional rather than decorative, no evident glass or heavy shadow treatment.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is form-led rather than button-led in the visible reference; where CTAs appear, they are likely single prominent actions near the hero or inside the form module, with restrained secondary CTA usage.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern evident in the provided reference HTML.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference HTML; no footer pattern inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible section; logo lockup in hero and icon-led bullet points, with content prioritized over imagery.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeated feature sections using label-eyebrow, headline, short descriptive paragraph, and feature lists; suited to long-form B2B education pages with modular topic blocks.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card immediately below the hero, with a strong section headline and multiple hidden tracking fields; indicates a conversion-oriented sidebar/card treatment adapted to mobile stacking.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-driven presentation with no clear motion system exposed in the HTML; any animation would be lightweight if present in external assets.
componentPatterns: Benefit bullet list with small icons
designNotes: B2B enterprise landing page structure optimized for clarity and conversion.
Content hierarchy is headline -> proof points -> form -> feature education.
The visual system should favor legibility, whitespace, and compact utility over illustration-heavy marketing.
Use repeated section framing to support long content volume without overwhelming users.

blueprint.heroFormBgRule: MANDATORY: Use heroBackgroundVideo as full-bleed autoplay muted loop video behind everything

mustHaveMoments: Brand/logo-led top strip with persistent visibility
Hero with concise value proposition and human professional visual element
Dominant trust band featuring business logos or logo-style proof first
Lead-capture form or trial CTA placed immediately after hero
Feature sections presented as readable stacked cards, not dense grids
Pricing/inclusions block with clear enterprise-oriented value framing
Testimonial section emphasizing operational outcomes and implementation ease
Sticky CTA strip near the bottom with footer
Final conversion prompt reinforcing free trial and enterprise relevance
avoidPatterns: Do not use a heavy numbered-statistic design as the main proof driver
Do not add extra lead magnets beyond the primary trial/get started CTA
Do not use grids inside grids for feature presentation
Do not crop hero visuals or overload the hero with too much text
Do not replace a human professional visual with abstract-only imagery if a person can be used
Do not omit the form, CTA strip, or footer
Do not let the page become invisible or delayed in rendering
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is an enterprise collaboration suite with long-form content, so the page should feel structured, credible, and conversion-focused rather than flashy. Since the strongest trust signal is logos, the design should foreground recognizable business proof immediately after the hero. The audience is solution-aware, so the strategy should clearly connect the product to productivity, collaboration, and secure unified communication without over-explaining. A split hero with a human professional visual supports trust and keeps the message readable. Stacked, airy sections improve scanability for the long content volume, while a persistent CTA and form preserve lead-gen momentum throughout the page.
